case_name: P. B. Roy v Union of India
respondent:
Union of India
Supreme Court of India

11 February 1972
Civil Appeal No. 2172 of 1968.
Appeal from the judgment and order dated August 10, 1967 of
the Delhi High Court in Letters Patent Appeal No. 97-D of
1965.
The Judgment was delivered by : M. Hameedullah, J.

facts: This is an appeal by grant of a Certificate of the Delhi High Court u/art. 132 read with Art. 133(1)(b) and (c) of the Constitution.
The Appellant had filed a petition u/art. 226 of the Constitution for quashing an order dated 10-3-1960 and had prayed for a consequential order also in the nature of a mandamus.
In 1955, the post of Editor, Publications Division, in the Department of Information and Broadcasting of the Government of India (hereinafter referred to as the 'Department'), was advertised.
The Appellant reported for duty on 1st August, 1956, as directed.
On 27-3-1957, the Appellant's probation was extended by three months.
Immediately thereafter, on 28-3-57, the Appellant's services were terminated under Rule 5 of the Central Civil Services (Temporary Service) Rules 1949,

On 16-2-1959, the President of India, in exercise of powers conferred by the Proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution of India, promulgated the Central Information Service Rules, 1959 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules), which came into force on 21-2-1959.
The Appellant assumed charge of the post thus assigned to him on the recommendation of the Union Public Service Commission.
The Appellant then made a representation, dated 11-3-1960 (Annexure 'E' to the Rejoinder Affidavit), against his appointment in Class II grade III post.
His last representation was made on 25-8-1962.

The learned Judge who had initially heard the petition had pointed out that the representation of the Appellant was first rejected on 29-7-1960 and that it did not matter that the petitioner had continued making subsequent representations.

The Division Bench which heard the Appeal of the Union of India was not inclined to interfere with the discretion of the learned Single Judge in rejecting the objection to the petition on the ground of delay.
issues: Whether the impugned order dated 10-3-1960 is valid and whether the Appellant's appointment in Class II grade III post is proper.
Whether the Rules created an altogether new service or merely transferred employees in existing posts to corresponding posts with new designations.
petitioner_arguments: The representation of the Appellant was first rejected on 29-7-1960 and that it did not matter that the petitioner had continued making subsequent representations.

The mere fact that the Department was reorganized and that the petitioner was to be fitted into an appropriate category by the procedure laid down in Rule 5 did not take away the effect, that is to say, the loss of his emoluments, of the procedure to which the petitioner had been subjected.
respondent_arguments: The Rules certainly did not provide for the continuance of any ex-cadre posts outside the new service introduced by the Rules.
Facts stated in the Affidavit of 26-7-1967 could have some bearing on the question whether there were two posts in the revised scale which could be considered as corresponding posts.
court_reasoning: The Division Bench held that the 'News and Information Cadre' of the Department, in which the Appellant was initially appointed, had been superseded by the cadres and grades constituted by the Rules of the new service.
It overruled the contention of the Petitioner that the effect of the Rules was merely to transfer employees in existing posts to corresponding posts with new designations.
holding: The Division Bench held that no question of demotion or reduction in rank, without observing the procedure laid down in Art. 311 of the Constitution, arose at all in the instant case.
